goldens.comment: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.
goldens.reasoning: Both say that removing the federated recovery-code credential in the authenticator flow will fail. C1 blames the local-storage removal API rather than the missing id. Still, it points to the same flow and the same symptom.

candidates: getCredential() now returns a federated recovery-code credential before checking local storage, which breaks the existing call path in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.isRecoveryAuthnCodeInputValid() - after a successful last-code use, the local-storage removal API will not remove the federated credential, so an exhausted recovery-code credential can remain undeleted in user storage and leave the user in stale state
